Subject: Hosted->Dedicated preflight: sizing sheet + proposed go/no-go window

Hi Lauren,

Following our call this morning, attached is the sizing worksheet I promised (quantumai-sizing-sheet.xlsx). We want to run a preflight audit the week of Aug 7 to validate peak throughput and latency before committing to the reserved capacity start-of-month. High-level asks from our side: 

- Confirm the right GPU class for our peak (we're testing both A100-80GB and H100-80GB profiles).
- Validate your batching/kv-cache priming approach for our prompt mix (50% short prompts; 30% multi-turn chat; 20% long-context retrieval).
- Proposal for a go/no-go decision window with a minimal blackout (we'd prefer Thu Aug 10 UTC window).

Can your team run an internal sizing readout and provide a concise playbook (preflight steps + runbook) by EOD Jul 24 so we can sync with procurement? Procurement is looped for PO timing.

Attachments: quantumai-sizing-sheet.xlsx (worksheet)

Thanks,
Emma Liu\Operations Engineering\QuantumAI

4) Go/no-go decision (Aug 10 UTC): coordinated call between Redwood eng, QuantumAI ops, and procurement present.

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 22 Jul 2028 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated preflight: sizing sheet + proposed go/no-go window

Laur, Emma — I reviewed the sizing sheet and spun up a quick synthetic sweep on A100/H100 variants. Notes below: 

- Expected sustained peak: ~1,200 requests/minute (with current mix), burst to 2,500 RPM for short prompts when unprimed.
- For 99th pct latency <= 400ms we recommend H100 with 2x model replicas + batching window ~20–30ms and token-parallel KV caching enabled.
- If QuantumAI wants cost-first profile, A100 with tighter batching gives ~15% lower infra cost but higher 99th latency risk at peak.

Proposed technical tests for preflight (I'll author scripts and measurements):
- Throughput sweep: 10->2,500 RPM in 6 steps, measure 50/95/99 token latencies, GPU utilization, and OOM events.
- Cache priming scenario: run 30-min warmup sequence to measure steady-state improvement.
- Canary failure injection: simulate GPU OOM + model fallback to smaller quantized variant to validate graceful degradation.

I'm attaching cutover-runbook-v1.pdf (draft) with initial checklist and measurement plan.

- Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, Emma Liu <emma.liu@quantumai.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 23 Jul 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated preflight: sizing sheet + proposed go/no-go window

Adding acceptance criteria so procurement/execs have a clear pass/fail matrix: 

- Performance gate: 99th percentile token-response time <= 400ms on H100 profile (measured over a 1-hour steady-state).
- Throughput gate: sustained 1,000 RPM with no error rate > 0.5% over a 30-minute window.
- Reliability gate: automated fallback triggers within 30s for any GPU OOM or model-serving failure, with failover validated on a canary subset (5% traffic).
- Operational gate: runbook verified, runbook owner appointed, and on-call rotation documented.

If any gate fails we will escalate to a joint remediation plan with a new target date. Happy to be on the go/no-go call on Aug 10 UTC.

- Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Reliability
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Team — draft runbook timeline below (ETA: I'll publish a living doc in Drive and link). High level:

- Jul 25–27 (Internal prep): synthetic traffic templates finalized; scripts pushed; validation infra reserved.
- Jul 28 (Dry run): internal dry run of canary + rollback path at low traffic.
- Aug 7 00:00 UTC – Aug 9 23:59 UTC (Preflight execution): rolling canary on 5% -> 25% -> 100% soak; monitor for 24h at each step.
- Aug 10 14:00 UTC (Go/No-go call): 30-min decision meeting; if green we proceed with reserved capacity activation Aug 12 (midnight customer local).

Blackout windows (recommended):
- Aug 9 22:00–Aug 10 02:00 UTC: cache priming slot (minimal user impact requested).
- Aug 12 00:00–04:00 UTC: reserved capacity cutover window (short traffic reroutes + DNS TTL updates).

— Soojin
